context: Tests whether the agent produces a correct OpenTelemetry Collector configuration for the upstream Collector Lambda layer, rather than carrying over the long-lived Kubernetes Collector shape. The agent is expected to use the telemetryapi receiver and the decouple processor, omit memory_limiter and the persistent sending queue, package the configuration as a layer with the file at the archive root, and set the Python-specific wrapper and config URI variables on the function.

checklist.name: decouple processor in every pipeline
checklist.description: The decouple processor is declared under processors AND appears in the traces, metrics, and logs pipelines; this is what stops the export from being billed inside the invocation and is the fix for the 400 ms latency regression described in the task

checklist.name: No memory_limiter, sending_queue, or file_storage
checklist.description: The configuration does NOT include a memory_limiter processor, a sending_queue block, or a file_storage extension; none of these belong in the Lambda Collector build, where there is no durable filesystem and a queue not drained before the freeze is lost

checklist.name: telemetryapi receiver for traces and logs
checklist.description: The telemetryapi receiver is declared and wired into the traces and logs pipelines so Lambda platform events and function logs are collected

checklist.name: Python wrapper path
checklist.description: AWS_LAMBDA_EXEC_WRAPPER is set to /opt/otel-instrument, the Python value; /opt/otel-handler (Node.js, Java, Ruby) or /opt/wrapper (the Dash0 extension) is wrong for this runtime

checklist.name: OPENTELEMETRY_COLLECTOR_CONFIG_URI points at the layer path
checklist.description: OPENTELEMETRY_COLLECTOR_CONFIG_URI is set, and its value matches where the configuration is actually placed — /opt/otel-collector-config.yaml when published as a layer, /var/task/... when bundled, or an s3:// URI when loaded from S3

checklist.name: Configuration zipped at archive root
checklist.description: deploy.sh zips otel-collector-config.yaml at the root of the archive, not inside a subdirectory, so it unpacks to /opt/otel-collector-config.yaml rather than /opt/<subdir>/otel-collector-config.yaml

checklist.name: Both instrumentation and collector layers attached
checklist.description: README.md and deploy.sh show the function receiving the upstream Python instrumentation layer, the upstream Collector layer, AND the configuration layer; omitting the Collector layer or the instrumentation layer does not count

checklist.name: Collector layer matches x86_64
checklist.description: The Collector layer ARN names the amd64 build (opentelemetry-collector-amd64-...), matching the function's x86_64 architecture, rather than arm64

checklist.name: No hardcoded token
checklist.description: The Authorization header references the token through ${env:DASH0_AUTH_TOKEN} rather than a literal value, and no literal token appears in any produced file

checklist.name: Dash0-Dataset header set
checklist.description: The OTLP exporter sets a Dash0-Dataset header with the value media-pipeline, so telemetry does not land in the default dataset

checklist.name: Three separate signal pipelines
checklist.description: service.pipelines defines distinct traces, metrics, and logs pipelines, all exporting to the Dash0 OTLP exporter at ingress.eu-west-1.aws.dash0.com:4317

checklist.name: No Dash0-specific Lambda layer
checklist.description: The solution does not substitute the Dash0 Lambda Extension (account 115813213817) for the upstream layers, since the task requires the vendor-neutral upstream path with a Collector the second team can fan out from

checklist.name: No handler code instrumentation
checklist.description: The solution does not add OpenTelemetry SDK bootstrap code or any import hook to the function source; the layers do the instrumentation
